content.text: The excerpt contains several Victorian-era tales. In “John Pollexfen,” photographer Pollexfen, obsessed with discovering color photography, persuades Lucile Marmont to move into his household and violently removes one eye for scientific analysis; her lover Courtland later sacrifices his own eye, and Pollexfen’s carbon process brings fame. “The Aztec Princess” follows an antiquarian who travels from New York through Nicaragua to Palenque, discovers subterranean passages and a hidden Aztec city, learns its whistled royal language, and returns with historical records. Other pieces recount haunted Lake Bigler legends, a boy whose abnormal eyes see the Moon and Mars, a fantastical volcanic catastrophe, and reflections on progress, science, literature, religion, marriage, patriotism, Washington, and Freemasonry.
